def: to commingle, i.e. (figuratively) to combine or assimilate

occurrences.text: For our comely parts have no need: but God hath tempered the body together, having given more abundant honour to that part which lacked:
For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
